tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תָּה בְחַרְתָּֽנוּ לְיוֹם הַסְּגִידָה
Tah Veḥartanu le-Yom haSgidah, an adaptation of the fourth berakhah of the Sigd festival musaf — by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Tah Veḥartanu le-Yom haSgidah, an adaptation of the fourth berakhah of the Sigd festival musaf — by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: You chose us from all peoples, loved us and desired us, and raised us over all tongues, and sanctified us with Your commandments, and brought us near, our Sovereign, to Your labor, and Your great and holy name over us You called, and You gave us, Cause our God, in love, festivals for joy, pilgrimages and seasons for happiness, this day of prostration, the day of accepting our covenant, a holy occurance, a remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.

But due to our sins we were exiled from our land and made distant from upon our ground, and we cannot offer up and be seen and bow before you and do our requirements in Your chosen house, the great and holy house of which Your name is called, due to the hand that was stretched out against Your Temple.

May it be willed before You, Cause our God and God of our ancestors, compassionate Sovereign, that You return and have compassion on us and on Your Temple in great compassion, and speedily rebuild it and greaten its glory.

Our Parent, our Sovereign, reveal Your glorious sovereignty upon us speedily and make known and bear us before the eyes of all flesh and bring near our dispersed from among the nations and gather our exiled from the ends of the earth and bring us to Ẓíōn Your city in cheer, and to Jerusalem Your holy Temple in eternal joy, and there we will do before You our required offerings, regular per their order and additional per their law.
But the addition for this Day of Prostration we will do as You wrote for us in Your Torah by the hands of Moshe Your servant, from Your holy mouth, as it is said:

And Moshe commanded the people on that day, quote: “These will stand to bless the people on Mt. Gerizim upon your crossing the Jordan: Shim’on and Levi and Yehuda and Yissachar and Yosef and Binyamin. And these will stand for the curse on Mt. ‘Eval: Reuven and Gad and Asher and Zvulun, Dan and Naftali. And the levites will announce and say to each Israelite person aloud.” (Deuteronomy 27:11–14)

Our God and God of our ancestors, compassionate Sovereign, have compassion on us; good one who does good, seek us, return to us in Your myriad compassions for the sake of the ancestors who did Your will; build Your house as it was and establish Your temple on its foundation that we may se its building and rejoice in its repair, and return the priests to their labor and the levites to their song and their hymn, and return Israel to their abode, and there we will ascend and be seen and bow down and prostrate before You on all the occasions of our times, as the matter is said in the words of Neḥemiah Your governor:

And they arose on their pulpits and read from the book of the Torah of the Cause their God a quarter of the day, and for a quarter of the day they confessed and prostrated themselves to the Cause their God. And getting up on the levite ascent, Yéshua’ and Bani, Qadmiel, Shvanya, Buni, Sherevya, Bani, Knani, and they cried in a loud voice to the Cause their God. And the levites, Yéshua’ and Qadmiel, Bani, Ḥashavnya, Sherevya, Hodiya, Shvanya, Ptaḥya, said: “Arise! Bless the Cause your God from eternity to eternity, and may Your honored name be blessed and exalted over all blessing and praise!” (Nehemiah 9:2–5)
And bring us, Cause our God, Your seasons’s blessing, for life and for peace, for joy and for happiness, as You desired and said to bless us.

Our God and God of our ancestors, may our remembrances and our accountings and the remembrance of our ancestors and the remembrance of the anointed son of David Your servant and the remembrance of Jerusalem Your holy city and the remembrance of all Your people the house of Israel ascend and come and reach and be seen and be desired and be heard and be accounted and be remembered before You for escape, for grace, for mercy and for compassion, for life and for peace on this Day of Prostration, the day of accepting our covenant. Remember us, Cause our God, on it for good, and account for us on it for blessing, and save us on it for life, and in a matter of salvation and compassion grace and have compassion on us and save is, for to You are our eyes, for a sovereign merciful and compassionate Deity are You.

Sanctify us in Your commandments and grant us a portion in Your law, sate us with Your good and make us rejoice in Your salvation and purify our hearts to serve You in truth, and Your word is true and enduring forever.
Blessed are You, who sanctifies Israel and the times.
